recall_prompt: Define both kinds of triangular matrix, and say which entries are zero in each.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Define upper triangular
steps.margin_note: First mark. Upper triangular means the zeros are BELOW the principal diagonal, so the numbers sit in the upper triangle. The entry condition is aᵢⱼ = 0 when i > j.
lines: A square matrix A = [aᵢⱼ] is called upper
triangular if every entry below the principal
diagonal is zero, that is aᵢⱼ = 0 when i > j.

recall.must_convey: That an upper triangular matrix is square with every entry below the principal diagonal equal to zero.
accept: upper triangular means all the entries below the principal diagonal are zero
a i j is zero whenever i is greater than j
the numbers sit on and above the diagonal
diagonal kinda unna entries anni zero unte upper triangular
zeros below the diagonal, values above it

steps.why: The name describes where the numbers are, not where the zeros are, so upper triangular has its zeros below the diagonal. Writing the entry condition aᵢⱼ = 0 when i > j removes any doubt about which side is meant.
common_mistakes: Putting the zeros above the diagonal and still calling it upper.
Requiring the diagonal entries to be non-zero, which is not part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Upper triangular: the numbers sit in the upper triangle, so the zeros are below the diagonal.

steps.label: Define lower triangular
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Lower triangular is the mirror case, aᵢⱼ = 0 when i < j. A matrix of either kind is called triangular, and its determinant is the product of the diagonal entries.
lines: A square matrix A = [aᵢⱼ] is called lower
triangular if every entry above the principal
diagonal is zero, that is aᵢⱼ = 0 when i < j.
A matrix of either kind is called triangular.

lines.text: ∴ A is triangular if it is upper or lower

recall.must_convey: That a lower triangular matrix has every entry above the principal diagonal equal to zero, and that either kind is called triangular.
accept: lower triangular means all the entries above the principal diagonal are zero
a i j is zero whenever i is less than j
a matrix that is upper or lower triangular is called triangular
diagonal paina unna entries anni zero unte lower triangular
zeros above the diagonal, values below it

steps.why: The two kinds are mirror images across the principal diagonal, and the transpose of an upper triangular matrix is lower triangular. A matrix that is both at once has zeros on both sides, which makes it a diagonal matrix.
common_mistakes: Naming only one kind when the question says triangular.
Giving a rectangular matrix as the example.
steps.memory_tip: Lower triangular is upper triangular reflected: transposing one gives the other.
